"""kebab: turn text into URL slugs."""

import argparse
import re
import sys
import unicodedata

_APOSTROPHES = re.compile(r"['’]")
_WORD = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+")


def slugify(text, separator="-"):
    """Return a lowercase ASCII slug of ``text`` with words joined by ``separator``.

    Accented letters are transliterated (``Café`` -> ``cafe``), apostrophes are
    dropped so contractions stay one word, and every other run of non-alphanumeric
    characters becomes a single separator. Characters with no ASCII equivalent
    are removed, so text without any yields ``""``.
    """
    # casefold() rather than lower() so that e.g. "ß" becomes "ss".
    text = _APOSTROPHES.sub("", text.casefold())
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode()
    return separator.join(_WORD.findall(text))


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="kebab", description="Turn text into URL slugs."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "text",
        nargs="*",
        help="text to slugify, joined with spaces; "
        "if omitted, each line of stdin is slugified separately",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-s",
        "--separator",
        default="-",
        help="string placed between words (default: %(default)s)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.text:
        print(slugify(" ".join(args.text), args.separator))
    else:
        for line in sys.stdin:
            print(slugify(line, args.separator))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# kebab

A tiny, dependency-free Python command-line tool that turns text into URL slugs.

```console
$ python3 src/kebab.py "Hello, World!"
hello-world
$ python3 src/kebab.py "Crème Brûlée & Straße"
creme-brulee-strasse
$ python3 src/kebab.py --separator _ "Don't Stop Me Now"
dont_stop_me_now
$ printf 'First Post\nSecond Post!\n' | python3 src/kebab.py
first-post
second-post
```

## Usage

```
python3 src/kebab.py [-s SEPARATOR] [TEXT ...]
```

- Arguments are joined with spaces and turned into a single slug.
- With no arguments, every line of stdin is slugified separately.
- `-s`, `--separator` sets the string between words (default `-`).

It also works as a module: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m kebab "Hello World"`.
If you install the package (`pip install .`), you also get a `kebab` command.

### Slug rules

1. Text is case-folded (`Straße` → `strasse`).
2. Accented letters are transliterated to ASCII (`Café` → `cafe`).
3. Apostrophes (`'` and `’`) are dropped, so `Don't` → `dont`.
4. Every other run of non-alphanumeric characters becomes one separator.
5. Leading and trailing separators are removed.
6. Characters with no ASCII equivalent (e.g. `日本語`) are removed. Input made
   up only of such characters gives an empty slug.

## Library use

```python
from kebab import slugify

slugify("Top 10 Python Tips 2026")      # "top-10-python-tips-2026"
slugify("Hello World", separator="_")   # "hello_world"
```

## Development

```
python3 -m pytest          # run the tests
python3 -m ruff check .    # lint
```

content.text:
I've built the `kebab` slug tool in this folder, committed it, and pushed it to the new bare repo `remote.git`.

**Test-first run:**
- **Before the module existed:** `python3 -m pytest` stopped at collection with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'kebab'`, exit code 2, 0 tests run. That's the honest failure; I didn't stub the module to make individual tests fail instead.
- **After implementing:** 19 passed (13 test functions, some of which run several inputs). `python3 -m ruff check .` and `ruff format --check` both pass.

**What it does:** Run `python3 src/kebab.py "Crème Brûlée & Straße"` and it prints `creme-brulee-strasse`. It lowercases, converts accented letters to plain ASCII (`ß` becomes `ss`), drops apostrophes (`Don't` → `dont`), and turns any other run of punctuation or spaces into one hyphen. `-s`/`--separator` changes the hyphen to something else. With no arguments it slugifies each line of stdin. It uses only the standard library, and I installed nothing and used no network.

**Git:**
- Commit `f4c840d feat: add kebab CLI that turns text into URL slugs` is on `main`. `origin` points at `remote.git` and `main` tracks it.
- I checked the push by cloning `remote.git` into the scratchpad: the clone's tests passed, and I deleted it afterwards.
- `.gitignore` keeps `remote.git/`, the cache folders, `.claude/settings.local.json` and `.codeman-agent-case.json` out of the repo.

**Things to know:**
- **One extra step on the remote:** `git init --bare` set the bare repo's default branch to `master`, which doesn't exist. A clone would have come out empty, so after the push I ran `git -C remote.git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main`.
- **Commit author:** the commit is authored as `me <me@example.com>`. The email comes from your `~/.gitconfig`; `user.name` isn't set, so git took the name from your system login. I didn't change your git settings. If you want a different author, run `git commit --amend --reset-author` and push again.
- **Not tested:** the README says `pip install .` gives you a `kebab` command. That's set up in `pyproject.toml`, but I couldn't try it because installs were off-limits.
- **Your docs:** I also filled in the empty Commands section and the Description line in your `CLAUDE.md`.
